pairs.why: A's chess table sits on a broad stepped pedestal and base that clearly carries the top, while B's slim post and thin top look less settled. The difference is small.
A's yoke runs from the truss clamp to pivot knobs on both sides of the lamp, but in B the left arm of the yoke ends on top of the barrel instead of at a pivot.
A's buttons have no labels, so the calculator could not be used, while B has a working, labeled number and operator keypad.
B's meteor is a believable cratered rock, while A's body is a soft blob with deep skull-like holes and floating flame droplets.
B is a buildable four-wheel covered wagon with a tongue at the front, while A's canvas has a round hole cut in its end and the shaft juts from the wrong side of a lopsided two-wheel cart.
B's loop is tied to the coil with a clear knot and has one finished end, while A's noose joins the coil at an unclear point and has a ferrule sitting in the middle of the loop.
B's cat figure has clearly separate front paws and a tail that wraps around its base, while A's legs and paws blur together. The difference is small.
A is a flat-on wall clock like the real card with all hands on the center pin, while B balances a round wall clock upright on its rim on the floor.
